source.how: get_computed_styles for the declared values; get_node_info / get_children for the laid-out rects, whose world coordinates are what `gaps` is computed from.

note: `border` is the USED width — Paper's canvas and Chromium both snap the sheet's declared 1.5px hairline to 1px at DPR 1, and every number below only adds up because of it. See scripts/lib/geometry-laws.mjs.

lawsNotDeclared.concentric-radius: Ghost has no fill and no border — there is no outer shape for the tab to be concentric with. Only the selected tab's own radius is observable, and the sheet draws it `--ui-radius-md` (LIK-0) while its unpainted siblings carry `--ui-radius-sm`; an unpainted radius is not a fact about the design.
lawsNotDeclared.track-is-the-sum-of-its-parts: The sheet's ghost rows are 26px, not the 24px the other two cases draw, because a 32px height was typed onto the frame and stretched them. The row wins — see deviations.

deviations.what: The sheet's ghost track is 32px tall with 26px rows; the implementation is 30px tall with 24px rows.
deviations.why: A Tab row is `min-h-6` in every variant — `pnpm design:primitives` reports it, and the two enclosed cases on this same sheet draw 24. The ghost frame's 26px rows are the consequence of a 32px height typed onto a frame whose parts add to 30, not a decision that ghost rows are taller than enclosed ones. The visible fact — the 3px inset around the selected fill — is identical either way, because ghost has no track to see.
